entry.title: Reign of Bloody Time
entry.summary:
Author: BadAshWolf

Rating: MatureLanguage: EnglishWords: 21,602Chapters: 12/25Kudos: 52

Summary: For years, he carved lines into the earth and runes into his own skin. Now, it is time to crack both open and drag the future back to his King. But, as warned in the days of old, nothing is brought back without a cost. He is a king-maker who has outlived his sovereign; a warlock who has finally stopped bartering with words and started bartering with existence. He will pay any price if it means his heart never goes where he cannot follow him again. Merlin burrows to a past that hasn't yet bled, and is no longer the bumbling servant Camelot remembers. He is something older, hungrier, and powerful beyond measure. This time, Arthur will not just wear a crown; Merlin will carve him into a god to match his own dark divinity. And if it takes a little blood to bind them together, to ensure what he is owed, who he earned, then Merlin will gladly teach his prince how to thirst for it. A long time-travel fix-it, a terrible and magnificent Merlin, an Arthur remade, and the breathless cost of devotion.

entry.title: He is half of my soul, as the poets say

Rating: MatureLanguage: EnglishWords: 70,009Chapters: 10/?Kudos: 244

Summary: “My lord?” Gaius called. Arthur swallowed hard before turning around. “Yes?” he replied, his voice strangely neutral, far too clear for someone who felt as though his chest were being crushed from the inside. “I need you to tell me in detail what happened” the physician said. The effort to remain professional was obvious, to keep from showing the despair that must have been consuming him at the sight of his nephew in such a state. “There’s nothing to tell” Arthur said far too quickly, as though he wanted to end the matter before it gained any weight. “He was completely normal one second, and the next he was groaning in pain, with his eyes…” he made a vague gesture with his hand, unable to finish. Giving it shape would make it real, and he was not sure he could bear it. What difference did it make now? He’s dead, a cruel part of his mind whispered. “Then his eyes rolled back and he… fainted.” ⸻ Or: where Merlin’s soul travels back in time while fighting in the midst of the Second World War, and, in the process, his body in Camelot dies for a few minutes, sending Arthur Pendragon to the verge of fainting.
